q: Is the paper's Theorem I.1 branch a_14 (bipartite, l,m both odd) = sp(2^{n-2})^{oplus 2} an off-by-one typo (should the exponent be n-1?), a hidden precondition (e.g. m >= some threshold), or a genuine mathematical error?
basis: Two independent DLA-saturation implementations (bit-symplectic Pauli tracking and explicit 2^n x 2^n matrix commutators with SVD-independence) both give dim(a_14^{K_{1,3}}) = 72 and dim(a_14^{K_{3,3}}) = dim(a_14^{K_{1,5}}) = dim(a_14^{H-graph n=6}) = 1056, matching 2 * dim sp(2^{n-1}) exactly for n=4 and n=6. The paper's Theorem I.1 asserts 2 * dim sp(2^{n-2}), which gives 20 and 272 respectively (differ by a factor of ~4). Every other branch of Theorem I.1 (101 of 105 test cases) matches numerically.
next_steps: Contact the paper's authors with a minimal counterexample (K_{1,3}, n=4: numerical dim 72, generator list, closure basis) and ask for confirmation or corrigendum. Verify by reading the arXiv v2/v3 source (LaTeX) directly to rule out an OCR/extraction artifact from pdftotext.

q: Is the numerical DLA in the a_14 BP-odd-odd branch isomorphic to sp(2^{n-1})^{oplus 2}, or is it a different Lie algebra of the same dimension (e.g. so(2^{n-1}+1)^{oplus 2})?
basis: For n=4 the dimension 72 equals both 2 * dim sp(8) = 2 * 36 and 2 * dim so(9) = 2 * 36; these are numerically indistinguishable. Dimension alone cannot pick the algebra type; a Cartan-classification-level invariant (rank, root system, signature of the Killing form) is required.
next_steps: Compute the Killing form on the closure numerically (skew-Hermitian generators, form the ad matrix, take trace(ad_X * ad_Y)) and diagonalize to check signature; alternatively find a Cartan subalgebra and count roots. Cross-check with an ODE-integration test: iterate the exponential map on random real linear combinations and see whether the orbit lies in Sp(2^{n-1}) or SO(2^{n-1}+1).

q: Does the '^{oplus 2}' factor in every a_k^G BP formula correspond to a Z_2 grading by a single collective spin-parity operator, and if so, which one for each (k, parity subcase)?
basis: Every BP formula in Theorem I.1 that involves an '^{oplus 2}' decomposition suggests a spin-parity operator P (e.g. Y^{oplus l} X^{oplus m} in Lemma IV.2's Q operator) that commutes with the DLA and splits its representation into two eigenspaces. The numerical closure preserves such parities but does not diagonalize them explicitly.
next_steps: For each mismatch case, find a Pauli operator P that commutes with every element of the closure and has (+/-1) eigenspaces of equal dimension. If found, verify the closure acts irreducibly on each eigenspace by computing the Schur count trace(rho(g)^2) over the closure; this would confirm the block-diagonal structure and locate whether the paper's dimension formula is exactly the block dimension times two.

q: For non-bipartite non-complete graphs beyond triangle+pendant, does Theorem III.9 (a_k^G = a_k^{K_n} for all NBP G with a vertex of degree > 2, k in {2,4,6,14}) hold for graphs that only marginally satisfy the degree hypothesis, e.g. a long cycle C_5 with a single chord (5 vertices, degree-3 vertex only where the chord attaches)?
basis: Our tests included exactly one NBP graph beyond K_n (triangle+pendant with a single degree-3 vertex), which matched K_4 for all k. Theorem III.9 asserts the equivalence for ALL such graphs, but the proof grows the graph edge-by-edge using L_3 ~_k K_3 (Lemma III.6), which requires triangles to already be present locally. Sparse NBP graphs (like a cycle+chord where the odd cycle is long) may need many more Lemma applications; verifying this at n=6, 7 numerically would test the theorem's robustness.
next_steps: Extend the verification battery with (i) C_5 + chord (n=5), (ii) K_4 minus one edge + pendant (n=5), (iii) a random 4-regular n=6 non-bipartite graph. Each should have a_k^G = a_k^{K_n} for k=2,4,6,14. Numerical mismatches would reveal missing preconditions.

q: How does the a_14 BP-odd-odd anomaly interact with the paper's Corollary I.2 statement that 'polynomial DLA scaling occurs only for a_0, b_0, b_1, b_3'? If the correct dimension is sp(2^{n-1})^{oplus 2} not sp(2^{n-2})^{oplus 2}, the exponent in the 4^n scaling changes from 4^{n-2}/2 to 4^{n-1}/2 — still exponential, but with a coefficient roughly 4x larger. Does this affect any downstream barren-plateau or trainability arguments the paper (or its citing works) rely on?
basis: Corollary I.2 uses only the O(4^n) scaling class, which is preserved under our proposed correction. However, papers building on Theorem I.1 for variance-of-gradient computations (barren plateaus) use the *exact* dimension in the denominator of the Var ~ 1/dim(DLA) formula. A factor-of-4 error in one branch would change the exact variance scaling by a factor of 4 for VQE circuits on odd-partition-size bipartite topologies.
next_steps: Reproduce the barren-plateau numerical experiment of one of the papers cited as [8, 9] in the introduction: sample random unitaries in the DLA lift, compute empirical Var of a single-Pauli observable's gradient, and compare against 1/dim(DLA) with both the paper's dimension and the corrected sp(2^{n-1}) dimension. Whichever matches empirically is the correct DLA.
